radius.$description: Fixed across the suite (hub ui-standard §2). Products choose values, never geometry.

space.$description: A 4px base on an 8px grid. The key is the multiple of 4px.

control.$description: Control heights (D-14): inputs, selects and buttons share one height per size, so a row of them lines up on one baseline. Each is a step of the space scale.

height.$description: Inputs, selects, buttons: 1px border, 12px padding, an 18px line (15px type at 1.2).

height-small.$description: Small buttons, small inputs and selects, and every control in the bar.

touch.$description: The floor for primary controls under 560px, where fingers are used (WCAG 2.5.5 at 44px).

breakpoint.$description: Viewport widths where layout changes (D-27). A media query cannot read a custom property, so these reach tokens.js (breakpoint) and Tailwind's @theme (--breakpoint-*, as phone:, max-phone: and so on), and components.css writes them as px literals that test/components.test.ts holds to these values. Each is the largest width that still counts as the smaller layout: write @media (max-width: <value>px) for 'on a phone'.

phone.$description: Under this the phone floors apply: primary controls 44 px (control.touch), one column, the bar sheds the person's address, tables drop the columns marked to go. The audit's PHONE_WIDTH.

tablet.$description: Under this an app's sidebar folds into a menu above main.

wide.$description: At and above this a page has its full width: content stops growing (about 1200 px), and the audit's and reviews' desktop width.

text.$description: Three ladders: a dense one for UI chrome and a reading one for page content, as Canonify's DESIGN-SURFACE has, and a display one for marketing pages (D-22). Hierarchy comes from weight on these steps, not from colour. Nothing under 11px.

chrome.$description: Dense UI: table heads, tags, meta, controls, data blocks (Canonify's ViewSpec ladder).

label.$description: Table header cells, tags, group labels. The floor.

content.$description: Pages: prose and headings. The steps are the account's (the reference, D-90), in the shape of Canonify's product-chrome ladder.

body.$description: Default running text. Canonify's chrome body is 14px; the account's 15px is kept.

marketing.$description: Landing pages, share images, decks and email headings (D-22, hub tick xl9): display sizes above content's h1. Running text on a marketing page stays on content's body.

eyebrow.$description: The short Space Mono label above a section heading.

lede.$description: The sentence or two under a hero or section heading.

h3.$description: Card and feature headings, the number's label on a figures row.

h1-min.$description: The hero headline on a phone.

h1.$description: The hero headline, once per page; the figures on a numbers row.

leading.$description: Line-height per step of the three type ladders (D-27), unitless so it scales with the size: leading.<ladder>.<step> beside text.<ladder>.<step>. A step's leading is for its running use (wrapping text, a label that may break); headings are tighter, running text looser. solid is 1, for one line in a box of its own: the wordmark, an avatar's initials, a count badge, an icon. A control's line box is not a leading: it is what the control's height leaves (--_control-line, D-14).

solid.$description: One line in a box of its own: the wordmark, initials, a count, an icon. Never text that may wrap.

chrome.$description: Dense UI. Tight, so a row of table cells or menu items stays compact.

figure.$description: A metric's value, one line, display weight.

content.$description: Pages. Running text at 1.55, the account's; headings tighten as they grow.

marketing.$description: Landing pages, decks, share images (D-22): the values brand/templates/deck.html uses. A two-line hero at 72 px and 1.05 is about 150 px tall.

font.$description: Families with fallbacks. The files are self-hosted by the product (never a font CDN, account D-17).
